name: Moab and Ammon
charge: Magnifying themselves against the Lord and against his people; rejoicing over the sanctuary when it was profaned
summary: Lot's two sons, neighbours to Israel from the wilderness on, are judged in Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Amos and Zephaniah for one long habit: pride against the Lord and gladness at Judah's ruin. Ammon ripped up the women with child of Gilead to enlarge its border; Moab said, Aha, against the house of Judah.
offense: We have heard of the pride of Moab; he is very proud: of his loftiness, and his arrogancy, and his pride, and the haughtiness of his heart. He shall be no more praised, because he hath magnified himself against the Lord. Of Ammon: because thou saidst, Aha, against my sanctuary, when it was profaned; and against the land of Israel, when it was desolate; and against the house of Judah, when they went into captivity. Amos: they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border.
judgment: Moab shall be destroyed from being a people, because he hath magnified himself against the Lord. Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days. Of Ammon: I will deliver thee to the men of the east for a possession, and Rabbah shall be a stable for camels; Zephaniah: Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, even the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation. Nebuchadnezzar came through both.

entries.commentary: This is the word of the Most High against Moab. Woe unto Nebo, for it is spoiled; Kiriathaim is confounded and taken. There shall be no more praise of Moab. In Heshbon they have devised evil against it: come, let us cut it off from being a nation. These are the Moabites, and God calls the so-called Chinese by that name.

A voice of crying goes up from Horonaim, spoiling and great destruction. Moab is destroyed, and her little ones cause a cry to be heard. Flee, save your lives, and be like the heath in the wilderness. There is no standing against the judgment that is coming.

Because thou hast trusted in thy works and in thy treasures, thou shalt also be taken. Chemosh their god goes into captivity with his priests and princes together. The spoiler comes upon every city, and no city escapes. The valley perishes and the plain is destroyed, as the Most High has spoken.
Cursed be he that doeth the work of the Lord deceitfully, and cursed be he that keepeth back his sword from blood. The work of the Most High is not to be done half-heartedly.

Moab has been at ease from his youth and settled on his lees, never emptied from vessel to vessel, never gone into captivity. Therefore his taste remained in him and his scent is not changed. The Most High will send wanderers to empty his vessels and break their bottles, and Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel.

How say ye, we are mighty and strong men for the war? Moab is spoiled, and his chosen young men are gone down to the slaughter, saith the King, whose name is the Lord of hosts. The calamity of Moab is near to come and his affliction hastens fast. All that know his name are to bemoan how the strong staff is broken.

The daughter that inhabits Dibon is told to come down from her glory and sit in thirst, for the spoiler of Moab comes upon her. The inhabitant of Aroer is to stand by the way and ask the one who flees, what is done. Moab is confounded, for it is broken down. Howl and cry, and tell it in Arnon that Moab is spoiled.

Judgment comes on the whole plain country, city by city, from Holon and Jahazah to Dibon, Nebo, Kiriathaim, Kerioth, and Bozrah, upon all the cities of Moab, far or near. The horn of Moab is cut off and her arm is broken. The strength of the nation is taken away by the Most High.

Make Moab drunken, for he magnified himself against the Lord, and he shall wallow in his own vomit and be in derision. The Most High asks, was not Israel a derision unto thee? Did the Lord not punish his own children? Then what makes the heathen think their time is not going to come? He punishes his own, so he will surely punish the wicked.

The pride of Moab is called out: exceedingly proud, his loftiness, his arrogance, and the haughtiness of his heart. For all that pride, these Moabites will go back to their proper place and serve the nation of Israel for what they have done. The wickedness of Moab against the children of God is real history the American Board of Education does not teach: enslaving us during the Tang Dynasty, feeding the ghettos, and building whole industries off our people. All of it will be manifested and answered for. -

The Most High declares he will howl and mourn for Moab, for the men of Kir-heres and the vine of Sibmah, because the spoiler is fallen upon the summer fruits and the vintage. Joy and gladness is taken from the plentiful field. He will cause to cease in Moab him that offereth in the high places and him that burneth incense to his gods. The idolatry is cut off with the people.

The heart of the Most High sounds like pipes for Moab, because the riches he has gotten are perished. Every head shall be bald and every beard clipped, with cutting upon the hands and sackcloth upon the loins. A good majority of Moab bald their heads and shave their faces rather than keep their beards, the same as the Mongolians right next door to them. There shall be lamenting generally upon the housetops of Moab.

Moab is broken like a vessel wherein is no pleasure. They howl, asking how it is broken down, and Moab becomes a derision and a dismay to all around him. He that judges shall fly as an eagle and spread his wings over Moab. The mighty men's hearts that day shall be as the heart of a woman in her pains, and Moab shall be destroyed from being a people because he magnified himself against the Lord.

Fear, the pit, and the snare are upon the inhabitants of Moab. He that flees the fear falls into the pit, and he that climbs out of the pit is taken in the snare; there is no escape from the years of their visitation. A fire comes forth out of Heshbon and devours the corner of Moab. Woe unto Moab, for thy sons and thy daughters are taken captives.

Yet the Most High will bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days. This has not happened yet, but it will come to pass, for he has spoken it and his word shall not return. Thus far is the judgment of Moab.

The word of the Most High comes against the Ammonites, the so-called Japanese, because they said Aha against His sanctuary when it was profaned, against the land of Israel when it was desolate, and against the house of Judah when they went into captivity. Because they clapped their hands, stamped their feet, and rejoiced in heart with all their despite against Israel, cheering our destruction, He will deliver them to the men of the east for a possession, cut them off from the people, and cause them to perish, that they may know He is the Lord.

Because Moab, the so-called Chinese, and Seir say that the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen, claiming Judah is no longer the Most High's chosen people, judgment is pronounced against them. The Most High will open the side of Moab from his frontier cities, the glory of the country, and deliver them to the men of the east along with the Ammonites so that the Ammonites be not remembered among the nations, and He will execute judgments upon Moab.

Because Edom, the so-called white man, dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance and greatly offended, the Most High will stretch out His hand upon Edom, cut off man and beast, and make it desolate from Teman, and they of Dedan shall fall by the sword. He will lay His vengeance upon Edom by the hand of His people Israel, and they shall do in Edom according to His anger and His fury. This is future prophecy that has not yet come to pass, for the Most High must first change our minds to act according to His anger to perform righteous recompense with our own hands. -

Because the Philistines dealt by revenge and took vengeance with a despiteful heart to destroy for the old hatred, never letting the feud go the way they always warred with us from the days of the judges, Samuel, Saul, and David, judgment comes upon them. The Most High will stretch out His hand upon the Philistines, cut off the Cherethims, destroy the remnant of the sea coast, and execute great vengeance with furious rebukes, that they may know He is the Lord when He lays His vengeance upon them.

The words of Amos, who was among the herdmen of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake. The Lord roars from Zion and utters his voice from Jerusalem, so that the habitations of the shepherds mourn and the top of Carmel withers. This chapter was read straight through without going precept upon precept.

For three transgressions of Damascus and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron. He will send a fire into the house of Hazael that shall devour the palaces of Benhadad, break the bar of Damascus, cut off the inhabitants of the plain of Aven and the sceptre from the house of Eden, and the people of Syria shall go into captivity unto Kir.

For three transgressions of Gaza and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they carried away the whole captivity to deliver them up to Edom. He will send a fire on the wall of Gaza that shall devour its palaces, cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod and the sceptre from Ashkelon, turn his hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish.

For three transgressions of Tyrus and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom and did not remember the brotherly covenant. He will send a fire on the wall of Tyrus that shall devour its palaces.

For three transgressions of Edom and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because Edom pursued his brother with the sword, cast off all pity, and kept his wrath forever. He will send a fire upon Teman that shall devour the palaces of Bozrah.

For three transgressions of the children of Ammon and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they ripped up the women with child of Gilead to enlarge their border. He will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah that shall devour its palaces, with shouting in the day of battle and a tempest in the day of the whirlwind, and their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together. --- Topics: [Esau and Edom](/encyclopedia/esau-and-edom) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant)

For three transgressions of Moab and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime. Moab today is the Chinese. He will send a fire upon Moab that shall devour the palaces of Kerioth, and Moab shall die with tumult, with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet, and he will cut off the judge and slay all the princes with him.

For three transgressions of Judah and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they despised the law of the Lord, did not keep his commandments, and their lies caused them to err after which their fathers walked. This is the reason we are in captivity even today. Going back to the Assyrian captivity, our forefathers were rebellious against the Most High's laws, did not want to keep the commandments, and wanted to worship idols. He will send a fire upon Judah that shall devour the palaces of Jerusalem.

For three transgressions of Israel and for four, the Most High will not turn away the punishment, because they sold the righteous for silver and the poor for a pair of shoes. That goes into oppression, and just like in today's time nobody wants to hear the righteous words of the Most High and keep the commandments; when you bring out the commandments you hear "what, I can't wear pants." They pant after the dust of the earth on the head of the poor, turn aside the way of the meek, and a man and his father go in unto the same maid to profane the Most High's holy name. There were men even in that time going in unto their father's wife, and you may find a TV show today promoting that behavior. They lay themselves down upon clothes laid to pledge by every altar and drink the wine of the condemned in the house of their god. -

Yet the Most High destroyed the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedar and who was strong as the oaks; he destroyed his fruit from above and his roots from beneath. The Amorite is another heathen nation. He brought Israel up from the land of Egypt, led them forty years through the wilderness to possess the land of the Amorite, and raised up their sons for prophets and their young men for Nazirites. You can use this to show that the children of Israel are the prophets of the Most High. But they gave the Nazirites wine to drink and commanded the prophets saying, prophesy not. That goes into lies and deceit, doing anything to stop the word of the Most High.

The Most High is pressed under them as a cart is pressed that is full of sheaves; therefore the flight shall perish from the swift, the strong shall not strengthen his force, and the mighty shall not deliver himself, because Israel will be in captivity. He that is courageous among the mighty shall flee away naked in that day; every possession you had will be stripped from you as you flee, the same way a robber coming to a bank strips everybody down and takes the goods.

Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired; before the decree bring forth, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you. Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord's anger.

Gaza shall be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation: they shall drive out Ashdod at the noon day, and Ekron shall be rooted up. The word of the Lord is against you; O Canaan, the land of the Philistines, I will even destroy thee, that there shall be no inhabitant. The coast shall be for the remnant of the house of Judah; they shall feed thereupon: for the Lord their God shall visit them, and turn away their captivity.

I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the revilings of the children of Ammon, whereby they have reproached my people, and magnified themselves against their border. Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah: the residue of my people shall spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them. This shall they have for their pride, because they have reproached and magnified themselves against the people of the Lord of hosts. He will stretch out his hand against the north, and destroy Assyria; and will make Nineveh a desolation, and dry like a wilderness. This is the rejoicing city that dwelt carelessly, that said in her heart, I am, and there is none beside me: how is she become a desolation!

Send the lamb to the ruler of the land from Sela to the wilderness, unto the mount of the daughter of Zion, for the daughters of Moab shall be at the fords of Arnon as a wandering bird cast out of the nest. Moab is told to take counsel, execute judgment, make her shadow as the night in the midst of the noonday, hide the outcasts, and not betray the one that wanders. She is asked to be a covert to the outcasts from the face of the spoiler. When the extortioner and spoiler are consumed out of the land, the throne shall be established in mercy, and one shall sit upon it in truth in the tabernacle of David, judging and seeking judgment and hasting righteousness.

We have heard of the pride of Moab, that he is very proud, of his haughtiness and pride and wrath, but his lies shall not be so. Therefore Moab shall howl for Moab, everyone shall howl. For the foundations of Kirhareseth they shall mourn, surely they are stricken. The fields of Heshbon languish and the vine of Sibmah, whose principal plants the lords of the heathen have broken down; her branches are stretched out, gone over the sea.

The prophet bewails the vine of Sibmah with weeping and waters Heshbon and Elealeh with his tears, for the shouting over the summer fruits and harvest is fallen. Gladness and joy are taken away out of the plentiful field; in the vineyards there is no singing nor shouting, and the treaders tread out no wine in their presses, for the Most High has made the vintage shouting to cease. The prophet's inward parts sound like a harp for Moab and for Kirharesh, and when Moab wearies himself upon the high place and comes to his sanctuary to pray, he shall not prevail.

This is the word the Most High has spoken concerning Moab since that time. But now the Most High speaks, saying that within three years, as the years of a hireling, the glory of Moab shall be contemned with all that great multitude, and the remnant shall be very small and feeble.

He that is wounded in the stones or hath his privy member cut off shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord. This law repeats what was already given: the priests' law in Leviticus lists the same blemishes that barred a man from approaching to offer the bread of his God, including him that hath his stones broken.

A bastard shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, even to his tenth generation: the children begotten of forbidden unions with the nations were shut out of the congregation. The prophets tie the bastard to Ashdod: a bastard shall dwell in Ashdod. Ashdod was one of the cities given to the tribe of Judah in the inheritance, but Israel did not drive out all the inhabitants and lost it. In the days of Nehemiah, Jews had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak in the Jews' language. Why is that? Because the mothers do the raising of the children.

An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord, even to their tenth generation, for ever. In the time of Nehemiah this very law was read out of the book of Moses in the audience of the people, and when they heard it our people separated from Israel all the mixed multitude whom they had intermarried with and had children with.

The reason for the ban: Ammon and Moab met not Israel with bread and with water in the way when they came forth out of Egypt, and hired Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor to curse them. The history is in Numbers: Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, was sore afraid because the people were many, and sent the elders of Moab and Midian with the rewards of divination to call Balaam to curse Israel. Nevertheless the Lord thy God would not hearken unto Balaam, but turned the curse into a blessing, because the Lord thy God loveth thee; therefore Israel was never to seek their peace nor their prosperity.

Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother: this was a temporary law. Edom broke the brotherly covenant; he did pursue his brother with the sword, did cast off all pity, his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever. Edom's hatred is a perpetual hatred: he shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, and as we see our people being slaughtered by Esau, that anger continues even to this very day. Thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian, because thou wast a stranger in his land: many brothers and sisters do not want to deal with that part and only want to deal with Edom, but Egypt likewise came under judgment for the violence against the children of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.

When the host goeth forth against thine enemies, then keep thee from every wicked thing: when Israel went to war, they were to keep themselves from every wicked thing. The example is Achan: Israel was warned in any wise to keep from the accursed thing, lest they make the camp of Israel a curse and trouble it, and Achan the son of Carmi of the tribe of Judah took of the accursed thing, the Babylonish garment, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against the children of Israel. Because of that trespass Israel could not stand before their enemies but turned their backs, for they were accursed; the Lord would not be with them any more except they destroyed the accursed from among them, and Achan and his family and all that belonged to him were destroyed and burned, and a heap set upon them, because he broke the covenant.

Any man that was not clean by reason of uncleanness that chanceth him by night went abroad out of the camp; when evening came he washed himself with water, and when the sun was down he came into the camp again.

There was a place without the camp to go forth abroad, and a paddle upon the weapon to dig and cover that which cometh from thee: to make it plain, if you had to ease yourself, you went outside the camp to do it. Verse 14 explains why: the Lord thy God walketh in the midst of thy camp, to deliver thee and to give up thine enemies before thee; therefore shall thy camp be holy, that he see no unclean thing in thee and turn away from thee. That is what we just read happened with Achan the son of Carmi: he brought an unclean thing into the camp, and the Most High turned from Israel in battle. God says he is in the midst of Israel and none else; the Lord would go before us and fight our battles, and that is why he wanted no unclean thing in the camp, for we are holy and the camp was to be holy.

There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel. A sodomite is the biblical word for a homosexual, and the whore of the daughters of Israel here is the same sin in the daughters, what we today would call lesbians. There is a heavy push in the world today for our men to be homosexuals and our sisters to be lesbians; popular entertainers are used to influence the younger generation to sin, just as young rappers were dressed in skirts and dresses until it became cool to be gay. This is what we have to bring our people back from: by being an example, the men being an example, the sisters being an example in the way they dress and carry themselves, and by having families, reinstituting a father and a mother in the divine order the Most High God established. Thou shalt not bring the hire of a whore or the price of a dog into the house of the Lord thy God, for even both these are abomination unto the Lord. Without are dogs: that is not the four-legged barking kind, but the other nations. Christ told a woman of another nation it is not meet to take the children's bread and cast it to dogs, and she said, Truth, Lord; and four-legged dogs did not pierce Christ's hands and feet, for the dogs that compassed him were the other nations, in that case the Romans.

Thou shalt not lend upon usury to thy brother, usury of money, of victuals, of any thing: when you read the definition of usury, that is interest. We are not to charge interest to each other when we loan each other anything. Unto a stranger thou mayest lend upon usury: the blessing is that Israel shall lend unto many nations and shall not borrow, the head and not the tail. That is our rightful place on the earth when we keep these commandments: we should lend unto them and may take usury upon what we lend to them, but we should not do that to our own people. The same law was already read in Exodus: if thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer.

verses.text: Make ye him drunken: for he magnified himself against the Lord: Moab also shall wallow in his vomit, and he also shall be in derision.
For was not Israel a derision unto thee? was he found among thieves? for since thou spakest of him, thou skippedst for joy.
O ye that dwell in Moab, leave the cities, and dwell in the rock, and be like the dove that maketh her nest in the sides of the hole’s mouth.
We have heard the pride of Moab, (he is exceeding proud) his loftiness, and his arrogancy, and his pride, and the haughtiness of his heart.
I know his wrath, saith the Lord; but it shall not be so; his lies shall not so effect it.
And Moab shall be destroyed from being a people, because he hath magnified himself against the Lord.
Fear, and the pit, and the snare, shall be upon thee, O inhabitant of Moab, saith the Lord.

He that fleeth from the fear shall fall into the pit; and he that getteth up out of the pit shall be taken in the snare: for I will bring upon it, even upon Moab, the year of their visitation, saith the Lord.

They that fled stood under the shadow of Heshbon because of the force: but a fire shall come forth out of Heshbon, and a flame from the midst of Sihon, and shall devour the corner of Moab, and the crown of the head of the tumultuous ones.
Woe be unto thee, O Moab! the people of Chemosh perisheth: for thy sons are taken captives, and thy daughters captives.
Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days, saith the Lord. Thus far is the judgment of Moab.
The word of the Lord came again unto me, saying,
Son of man, set thy face against the Ammonites, and prophesy against them;

And say unto the Ammonites, Hear the word of the Lord God; Thus saith the Lord God; Because thou saidst, Aha, against my sanctuary, when it was profaned; and against the land of Israel, when it was desolate; and against the house of Judah, when they went into captivity;

Behold, therefore I will deliver thee to the men of the east for a possession, and they shall set their palaces in thee, and make their dwellings in thee: they shall eat thy fruit, and they shall drink thy milk.
And I will make Rabbah a stable for camels, and the Ammonites a couchingplace for flocks: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.
For thus saith the Lord God; Because thou hast clapped thine hands, and stamped with the feet, and rejoiced in heart with all thy despite against the land of Israel;

Behold, therefore I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and will deliver thee for a spoil to the heathen; and I will cut thee off from the people, and I will cause thee to perish out of the countries: I will destroy thee; and thou shalt know that I am the Lord.
Thus saith the Lord God; Because that Moab and Seir do say, Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen;
Therefore, behold, I will open the side of Moab from the cities, from his cities which are on his frontiers, the glory of the country, Beth–jeshimoth, Baal–meon, and Kiriathaim,
Unto the men of the east with the Ammonites, and will give them in possession, that the Ammonites may not be remembered among the nations.
And I will execute judgments upon Moab; and they shall know that I am the Lord.

Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border:
But I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it shall devour the palaces thereof, with shouting in the day of battle, with a tempest in the day of the whirlwind:
And their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together, saith the Lord.
Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Moab, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime:
But I will send a fire upon Moab, and it shall devour the palaces of Kerioth: and Moab shall die with tumult, with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet:
And I will cut off the judge from the midst thereof, and will slay all the princes thereof with him, saith the Lord.
I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the revilings of the children of Ammon, whereby they have reproached my people, and magnified themselves against their border.

Therefore as I live, saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, even the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation: the residue of my people shall spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them.
This shall they have for their pride, because they have reproached and magnified themselves against the people of the Lord of hosts.
The Lord will be terrible unto them: for he will famish all the gods of the earth; and men shall worship him, every one from his place, even all the isles of the heathen.
We have heard of the pride of Moab; he is very proud: even of his haughtiness, and his pride, and his wrath: but his lies shall not be so.
Therefore shall Moab howl for Moab, every one shall howl: for the foundations of Kir–hareseth shall ye mourn; surely they are stricken.
An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord; even to their tenth generation shall they not enter into the congregation of the Lord for ever:
Because they met you not with bread and with water in the way, when ye came forth out of Egypt; and because they hired against thee Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor of Mesopotamia, to curse thee.

For was not Israel a derision unto thee? was he found among thieves? for since thou spakest of him, thou skippedst for joy.
O ye that dwell in Moab, leave the cities, and dwell in the rock, and be like the dove that maketh her nest in the sides of the hole’s mouth.
We have heard the pride of Moab, (he is exceeding proud) his loftiness, and his arrogancy, and his pride, and the haughtiness of his heart.
I know his wrath, saith the Lord; but it shall not be so; his lies shall not so effect it.
And Moab shall be destroyed from being a people, because he hath magnified himself against the Lord.
Fear, and the pit, and the snare, shall be upon thee, O inhabitant of Moab, saith the Lord.

He that fleeth from the fear shall fall into the pit; and he that getteth up out of the pit shall be taken in the snare: for I will bring upon it, even upon Moab, the year of their visitation, saith the Lord.

They that fled stood under the shadow of Heshbon because of the force: but a fire shall come forth out of Heshbon, and a flame from the midst of Sihon, and shall devour the corner of Moab, and the crown of the head of the tumultuous ones.
Woe be unto thee, O Moab! the people of Chemosh perisheth: for thy sons are taken captives, and thy daughters captives.
Yet will I bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days, saith the Lord. Thus far is the judgment of Moab.
The word of the Lord came again unto me, saying,
Son of man, set thy face against the Ammonites, and prophesy against them;

And say unto the Ammonites, Hear the word of the Lord God; Thus saith the Lord God; Because thou saidst, Aha, against my sanctuary, when it was profaned; and against the land of Israel, when it was desolate; and against the house of Judah, when they went into captivity;

Behold, therefore I will deliver thee to the men of the east for a possession, and they shall set their palaces in thee, and make their dwellings in thee: they shall eat thy fruit, and they shall drink thy milk.
And I will make Rabbah a stable for camels, and the Ammonites a couchingplace for flocks: and ye shall know that I am the Lord.
For thus saith the Lord God; Because thou hast clapped thine hands, and stamped with the feet, and rejoiced in heart with all thy despite against the land of Israel;

Behold, therefore I will stretch out mine hand upon thee, and will deliver thee for a spoil to the heathen; and I will cut thee off from the people, and I will cause thee to perish out of the countries: I will destroy thee; and thou shalt know that I am the Lord.
Thus saith the Lord God; Because that Moab and Seir do say, Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen;
Therefore, behold, I will open the side of Moab from the cities, from his cities which are on his frontiers, the glory of the country, Beth–jeshimoth, Baal–meon, and Kiriathaim,
Unto the men of the east with the Ammonites, and will give them in possession, that the Ammonites may not be remembered among the nations.
And I will execute judgments upon Moab; and they shall know that I am the Lord.

Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border:
But I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it shall devour the palaces thereof, with shouting in the day of battle, with a tempest in the day of the whirlwind:
And their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together, saith the Lord.
Thus saith the Lord; For three transgressions of Moab, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he burned the bones of the king of Edom into lime:
But I will send a fire upon Moab, and it shall devour the palaces of Kerioth: and Moab shall die with tumult, with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet:
And I will cut off the judge from the midst thereof, and will slay all the princes thereof with him, saith the Lord.
I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the revilings of the children of Ammon, whereby they have reproached my people, and magnified themselves against their border.

Therefore as I live, saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, even the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation: the residue of my people shall spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them.
This shall they have for their pride, because they have reproached and magnified themselves against the people of the Lord of hosts.
The Lord will be terrible unto them: for he will famish all the gods of the earth; and men shall worship him, every one from his place, even all the isles of the heathen.
We have heard of the pride of Moab; he is very proud: even of his haughtiness, and his pride, and his wrath: but his lies shall not be so.
Therefore shall Moab howl for Moab, every one shall howl: for the foundations of Kir–hareseth shall ye mourn; surely they are stricken.
An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord; even to their tenth generation shall they not enter into the congregation of the Lord for ever:
Because they met you not with bread and with water in the way, when ye came forth out of Egypt; and because they hired against thee Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor of Mesopotamia, to curse thee.
